categories.name: Identity
categories.blurb: How well you verify who users are and control what each identity can reach across your environment.

categories.name: Devices
categories.blurb: How thoroughly you inventory, secure, and continuously vet the devices that connect to your resources.

categories.name: Networks
categories.blurb: How much you segment, encrypt, and dynamically control traffic instead of trusting the internal network.

categories.name: Applications and Workloads
categories.blurb: How you secure access to applications and build protections into their development and runtime.

categories.name: Data
categories.blurb: How well you inventory, classify, encrypt, and govern access to your data wherever it lives.

categories.name: Visibility and Analytics
categories.blurb: How completely you collect, correlate, and analyze security signals to drive decisions.

categories.name: Automation and Orchestration
categories.blurb: How much of your security response and policy enforcement runs automatically and in a coordinated way.

categories.name: Governance
categories.blurb: How consistently you define, enforce, and measure cybersecurity policy across every pillar.

questions.text: Do you require multi-factor authentication for user logins instead of relying on passwords alone?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Identity
questions.why: Passwords alone are easily phished, guessed, or reused, letting attackers log in as legitimate users.
questions.fix: Turn on MFA for user sign-ins, starting with administrators and remote access.

questions.text: Have you started consolidating user accounts into a central identity store rather than separate logins per system?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Identity
questions.why: Scattered per-system accounts create orphaned logins and blind spots that are hard to secure or revoke.
questions.fix: Stand up a central identity provider and begin migrating applications to authenticate against it.

questions.text: Do you automate parts of the account lifecycle, such as provisioning and deprovisioning, rather than doing it all by hand?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Identity
questions.why: Manual account handling leaves stale accounts active long after a person changes roles or leaves.
questions.fix: Connect your identity provider to HR or directory events so joins, moves, and leaves update access automatically.

questions.text: Do you enforce phishing-resistant MFA across most of your enterprise applications?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Identity
questions.why: SMS and push-based MFA can be bypassed by phishing and fatigue attacks that phishing-resistant methods block.
questions.fix: Roll out FIDO2 security keys or certificate-based authentication and require them for sensitive apps.

questions.text: Does your access system automatically adjust a user's privileges based on real-time risk signals?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Identity
questions.why: Static privileges stay open even when a session shows signs of compromise or unusual behavior.
questions.fix: Configure conditional access policies that step up authentication or limit access when risk scores rise.

questions.text: Do you grant access using just-in-time, just-enough-access rather than leaving standing privileges in place?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Identity
questions.why: Standing privileged access is a large attack surface that adversaries target to move and escalate.
questions.fix: Adopt privileged access management that grants time-bound, approval-based elevation only when needed.

questions.text: Does your environment continuously validate identity and revoke access automatically the moment risk changes?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Identity
questions.why: Trust granted once at login can be abused for the whole session if it is never re-checked.
questions.fix: Enable continuous access evaluation so token validity reacts to risk, revocation, and posture changes in near real time.

questions.text: Do you maintain an inventory of most devices that connect to your network?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Devices
questions.why: You cannot protect or make access decisions about devices you do not know exist.
questions.fix: Deploy asset discovery and a device inventory that captures every endpoint reaching your resources.

questions.text: Do you check a device's basic security posture before granting it access to resources?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Devices
questions.why: Unpatched or misconfigured devices become an easy foothold when allowed to connect unchecked.
questions.fix: Require a simple posture check, such as OS version and disk encryption, at the point of access.

questions.text: Have you deployed endpoint protection or detection tooling on most of your devices?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Devices
questions.why: Without endpoint tooling, malware and intrusions on a device can go unnoticed and spread.
questions.fix: Install and centrally manage an endpoint detection and response agent across your fleet.

questions.text: Does your access system factor real-time device compliance and health into each access decision?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Devices
questions.why: A device that was compliant yesterday may be out of date or compromised at the moment of access.
questions.fix: Integrate device compliance signals into your access policies so noncompliant devices are blocked or limited.

questions.text: Do you centrally manage and enforce security configurations across most enterprise devices?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Devices
questions.why: Inconsistent, locally managed settings drift into weak configurations that attackers exploit.
questions.fix: Use a unified endpoint management platform to push and enforce baseline security policies.

questions.text: Do your devices continuously report their security status so access can adjust dynamically?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Devices
questions.why: Point-in-time checks miss changes in device health that occur during an active session.
questions.fix: Enable continuous device telemetry that feeds live posture into your access engine.

questions.text: Is device threat detection integrated with automated response that isolates compromised devices without manual steps?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Devices
questions.why: Manual isolation is too slow to stop a compromised device from spreading to other systems.
questions.fix: Connect endpoint detection to automated playbooks that quarantine a device the instant a threat is confirmed.

questions.text: Have you divided your network into separate segments rather than running one flat network?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Networks
questions.why: A flat network lets an attacker who breaches one system reach everything else unimpeded.
questions.fix: Split your network into segments by function or sensitivity and control traffic between them.

questions.text: Do you encrypt at least some internal network traffic instead of sending it in the clear?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Networks
questions.why: Cleartext internal traffic can be sniffed or altered by anyone who gains a network foothold.
questions.fix: Enable TLS for internal services and start retiring unencrypted protocols.

questions.text: Do you manage and monitor traffic at defined network boundaries?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Networks
questions.why: Without controlled boundaries you cannot see or stop malicious inbound and outbound traffic.
questions.fix: Place firewalls and monitoring at ingress and egress points and log the traffic they see.

questions.text: Have you implemented microsegmentation to isolate individual workloads or applications?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Networks
questions.why: Coarse segments still allow broad lateral movement between systems that never need to talk.
questions.fix: Apply per-workload policies so each application only accepts the connections it actually requires.

questions.text: Is most of your network traffic, including internal traffic, encrypted by default?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Networks
questions.why: Partial encryption leaves gaps where sensitive traffic can still be intercepted.
questions.fix: Make encryption the default for all services and flag any remaining cleartext flows for remediation.

questions.text: Are network access policies enforced dynamically based on real-time risk and application needs?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Networks
questions.why: Static network rules cannot respond to emerging threats or changing conditions fast enough.
questions.fix: Adopt policy-driven networking that adjusts access based on live risk and identity signals.

questions.text: Does your network encrypt traffic end to end and adapt segmentation automatically as conditions change?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Networks
questions.why: Manual segmentation and partial encryption cannot keep pace with dynamic, distributed environments.
questions.fix: Use software-defined segmentation with pervasive encryption that reconfigures automatically to workload changes.

questions.text: Do you require authentication and access control before users can reach internal applications?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Applications and Workloads
questions.why: Applications reachable without authentication are open doors for anyone who finds them.
questions.fix: Put every internal application behind identity-based authentication and authorization.

questions.text: Do you run security testing on applications at some point before releasing them?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Applications and Workloads
questions.why: Shipping untested code lets known vulnerability classes reach production where attackers find them.
questions.fix: Add basic static and dependency scanning as a gate before releases go live.

questions.text: Have you begun making applications available securely without requiring a traditional VPN into the network?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Applications and Workloads
questions.why: VPN access places users on the internal network, granting far more reach than any single app needs.
questions.fix: Publish key applications through an identity-aware proxy so users reach only the app, not the network.

questions.text: Do you enforce access to applications based on context such as user, device, and risk rather than network location?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Applications and Workloads
questions.why: Trusting anyone on the internal network lets a single breach reach many applications at once.
questions.fix: Configure context-aware access policies that evaluate identity, device health, and risk per request.

questions.text: Is application security testing integrated into your continuous integration and delivery pipeline?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Applications and Workloads
questions.why: Testing only at the end lets vulnerabilities accumulate and ship before anyone catches them.
questions.fix: Embed automated security scans into every build so issues fail the pipeline early.

questions.text: Do application access decisions continuously adapt to real-time risk throughout each session?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Applications and Workloads
questions.why: Access granted at login can be abused if the session is never re-evaluated as risk shifts.
questions.fix: Enable continuous, risk-adaptive authorization that can downgrade or cut off access mid-session.

questions.text: Are application protections and threat monitoring automated across the full development and runtime lifecycle?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Applications and Workloads
questions.why: Gaps between build-time and runtime security let threats slip through unmonitored once apps are live.
questions.fix: Unify pipeline scanning with runtime protection and automated response for a continuous security loop.

questions.text: Have you begun inventorying where your most important data is stored?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Data
questions.why: Data you have not located cannot be protected, and unknown stores are common breach sources.
questions.fix: Run discovery to map where sensitive data lives across systems, cloud, and endpoints.

questions.text: Do you classify at least some data by sensitivity so it can be protected accordingly?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Data
questions.why: Without classification, sensitive and public data get the same weak protection.
questions.fix: Define a simple sensitivity scheme and label your highest-value data first.

questions.text: Do you encrypt sensitive data when it is stored at rest?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Data
questions.why: Unencrypted stored data is fully exposed if a disk, backup, or database is stolen or copied.
questions.fix: Turn on encryption at rest for databases, storage, and backups holding sensitive data.

questions.text: Do you apply automated data classification and tagging across most of your repositories?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Data
questions.why: Manual labeling cannot keep up with data volume, so much sensitive data goes untagged and unprotected.
questions.fix: Deploy tools that scan and automatically tag data by sensitivity as it is created and moved.

questions.text: Do you control access to data based on its sensitivity and the requester's context?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Data
questions.why: Broad, role-only access lets far more people reach sensitive data than actually need it.
questions.fix: Tie data access policies to classification labels plus user, device, and risk context.

questions.text: Is access to data governed by dynamic policies that respond to real-time risk?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Data
questions.why: Static data permissions stay open even when a session or account shows clear signs of compromise.
questions.fix: Enforce data access through a policy engine that adjusts or blocks access as risk signals change.

questions.text: Do you encrypt data in transit, at rest, and in use with continuous monitoring for unauthorized access?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Data
questions.why: Data left unprotected in any state, especially while in use, gives attackers a route to exfiltrate it.
questions.fix: Extend encryption to data in use with technologies like confidential computing and monitor all access continuously.

questions.text: Do you collect and centralize logs from most of your systems rather than leaving them siloed?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Visibility and Analytics
questions.why: Logs scattered across systems make it nearly impossible to spot an attack that crosses them.
questions.fix: Forward logs from your key systems into a central logging or SIEM platform.

questions.text: Do you actively monitor for security events across your enterprise environment?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Visibility and Analytics
questions.why: Collected logs provide no protection if no one is watching them for signs of attack.
questions.fix: Set up alerting on your central logs and assign someone to triage the events.

questions.text: Do you correlate data across identity, devices, networks, and applications to detect threats?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Visibility and Analytics
questions.why: Single-source alerts miss multi-stage attacks that only appear when signals are combined.
questions.fix: Use correlation rules or analytics that join events across pillars into unified detections.

questions.text: Do your analytics feed risk signals into access and policy decisions?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Visibility and Analytics
questions.why: Insights that never reach policy enforcement leave known risks free to be exploited.
questions.fix: Wire your analytics output into access policies so detected risk changes what users can do.

questions.text: Do you use automated analytics and machine-driven detection for near real-time situational awareness?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Visibility and Analytics
questions.why: Purely manual analysis is too slow to catch fast-moving threats before damage is done.
questions.fix: Adopt behavioral analytics and machine learning detections that surface anomalies automatically.

questions.text: Does comprehensive, continuous visibility span both your internal and externally hosted resources?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Visibility and Analytics
questions.why: Blind spots in cloud or third-party environments are exactly where attackers prefer to operate.
questions.fix: Extend telemetry collection and monitoring to cloud, SaaS, and partner-hosted resources.

questions.text: Have you automated at least some routine security responses instead of handling every incident manually?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Automation and Orchestration
questions.why: Fully manual response is slow and inconsistent, giving threats time to spread.
questions.fix: Automate a few common, low-risk responses such as disabling an account or blocking an indicator.

questions.text: Do you use defined playbooks to guide and speed up incident response?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Automation and Orchestration
questions.why: Ad hoc response leads to missed steps and slow reactions under pressure.
questions.fix: Document step-by-step playbooks for your most common incident types.

questions.text: Do your security tools share information and coordinate responses across different pillars?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Automation and Orchestration
questions.why: Disconnected tools force analysts to bridge gaps by hand, slowing containment.
questions.fix: Integrate your tools through a SOAR platform or shared APIs so they act on each other's signals.

questions.text: Do you automatically enforce and update security policies based on predefined triggers?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Automation and Orchestration
questions.why: Policies that only change through manual work drift out of date as conditions evolve.
questions.fix: Define triggers that automatically apply or tighten policies when specific conditions are met.

questions.text: Does your environment respond to threats automatically in near real time with minimal human intervention?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Automation and Orchestration
questions.why: Human-in-the-loop response cannot match the speed of automated attacks.
questions.fix: Expand trusted playbooks so confirmed threats are contained automatically, with humans reviewing after the fact.

questions.text: Are security workflows fully orchestrated across all pillars with dynamic, self-adjusting policies?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Automation and Orchestration
questions.why: Partial orchestration leaves seams between pillars that attackers exploit during an incident.
questions.fix: Unify orchestration end to end so policies and responses adapt automatically across every pillar.

questions.text: Have you documented cybersecurity policies that define how access and resources are protected?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Governance
questions.why: Without written policy, security decisions are inconsistent and impossible to hold anyone to.
questions.fix: Write down baseline access and protection policies and share them with the organization.

questions.text: Have you begun enforcing your security policies consistently rather than leaving it to individual teams?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Governance
questions.why: Policies enforced unevenly leave predictable gaps that attackers seek out.
questions.fix: Assign clear ownership and start applying core policies uniformly across teams.

questions.text: Do you enforce security policies centrally and consistently across most pillars?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Governance
questions.why: Pillar-by-pillar governance creates conflicting rules and coverage gaps between them.
questions.fix: Manage policy from a central point that applies consistently across identity, devices, networks, apps, and data.

questions.text: Do you track compliance with your zero trust policies using measurable metrics?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Governance
questions.why: Without metrics you cannot tell where policy is being followed or where risk is piling up.
questions.fix: Define key metrics and dashboards that report policy compliance and exceptions.

questions.text: Are governance policies enforced automatically and updated dynamically as risk changes?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Governance
questions.why: Manually maintained governance lags behind fast-changing environments and emerging threats.
questions.fix: Adopt policy-as-code so governance is enforced automatically and adjusts to real-time risk.

questions.text: Does your governance extend across the entire enterprise, including externally hosted and third-party resources?
references: CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model 2.0: Governance
questions.why: Ungoverned cloud and partner resources become weak links outside your control.
questions.fix: Bring externally hosted and third-party resources under the same enterprise policy and oversight.
